pins.name: GPIO12
pins.label: GPIO12 (Button)
pins.notes:
BUTTON_A — onboard general-purpose pushbutton, active-low. Confirmed via rp-hal-boards pimoroni-plasma-2040 lib.rs ('GPIO 12 is connected to button A, active low'), corroborated by shop.pimoroni.com ('three useful buttons') and pimoroni-pico's rgb-led-and-buttons.py example (Button(plasma2040.BUTTON_A)). Full digital_input/digital_output/pwm_output retained (ordinary GPIO wired to a switch to GND, no special circuitry documented), matching adafruit_feather_scorpio's GPIO7 BOOT-button precedent.
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO14
pins.label: GPIO14
pins.notes:
CLK — screw-terminal clock line for external APA102/Dotstar LED strip output. Confirmed general-purpose GPIO (not a dedicated/fixed silicon function) via rp-hal-boards lib.rs ('GPIO 14 is connected to CLK for APA102 only') and learn.pimoroni.com's CircuitPython example (board.CLK passed directly into the user's own dotstar.DotStar() library call), matching the adafruit_feather_scorpio GPIO16-23 'general-purpose, merely well-suited to strip-driving' precedent — no strip-specific capability tag exists in this repo's vocabulary, and none is warranted since this pin does not drive board-owned hardware. Not declared at all in this board's own pins_arduino.h (no PIN_ alias); added here purely via chipGpios, matching the general 'GPIO absent from pins_arduino.h but present in chipGpios' mechanism (see pimoroni_tiny2040 GPIO23 precedent).
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO15
pins.label: GPIO15
pins.notes:
DAT — screw-terminal data line for external WS2812/Neopixel and APA102/Dotstar LED strip output. This is this board's own pins_arduino.h PIN_NEOPIXEL(15) alias, but despite the name it is NOT an onboard NeoPixel — it drives the external strip connector, confirmed general-purpose via rp-hal-boards lib.rs ('GPIO 15 is connected to DAT for Apa102 and Ws2812'), learn.pimoroni.com's CircuitPython examples (board.DATA / board.NEOPIXEL passed into the user's own strip-driver library call), and forums.pimoroni.com's Plasma 2040 pinouts thread (screw terminal 'DA' = GPIO15). No led_neopixel tag applied — that tag is reserved for a board's own onboard addressable LED (e.g. adafruit_feather_scorpio GPIO4), which this pin is not.
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.label: GPIO16 (Led Red active low)
pins.notes:
LED_R — onboard status RGB LED red channel, active-low. Confirmed via rp-hal-boards lib.rs ('GPIO 16 is red LED, active low'), corroborated by multiple independent sources (shop.pimoroni.com, pimoroni-pico's rgb-led-and-buttons.py RGBLED(plasma2040.LED_R, ...)). digital_input dropped to match this repo's established led_r/g/b_low precedent for dedicated onboard RGB status LEDs (pimoroni_tiny2040 GPIO18); pwm_output kept since arduino-pico's analogWrite() works on any RP2040 GPIO, enabling brightness/colour dimming.

pins.name: GPIO23
pins.label: GPIO23 (Button)
pins.notes:
USER_SW — third onboard button, doubles as the BOOT-select switch but confirmed freely reusable as a plain input by running application code (rp-hal-boards lib.rs: 'GPIO 23 is connected to the USER_SW, the BOOT button, active low'; pimoroni-pico's rgb-led-and-buttons.py: Button(plasma2040.USER_SW) read identically to BUTTON_A/B). No vendor source documents diode isolation or any other special circuitry for this pin (unlike the Pimoroni Tiny 2040's explicitly diode-protected BOOTSEL line), so full digital_input/digital_output/pwm_output is retained alongside button, matching adafruit_feather_scorpio's GPIO7 BOOT-button precedent rather than pimoroni_tiny2040's more conservative input-only GPIO23 treatment.
Check if available on board
